Snapshot = project 63436ae6 + Mathlib 25730c7c; the snapshot Contract is byte-identical to the workspace Contract and Submission. Mathlib has no varifold theory, so the Ch. 8 objects come from the frozen contract and the pinned SimonGMT package.

subproblem.title: Borel measurability of the upper/lower n-densities and their level sets (Simon Ch. 1, 3.2; parent step 8)
subproblem.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ and μ an s-finite Borel measure on ℝ^N. Then x ↦ limsup_{ρ↓0} μ(B̄_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n) and x ↦ liminf_{ρ↓0} μ(B̄_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n) are Borel functions ℝ^N → [0,∞], and for every c ∈ [0,∞] the set {x : Θ^n(μ,x) exists and equals c} is a Borel set.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclidean N)) [SFinite μ], Measurable (fun x ↦ limsup (densityRatio n μ x) (𝓝[>] 0)) ∧ Measurable (fun x ↦ liminf (densityRatio n μ x) (𝓝[>] 0)) ∧ ∀ c : ℝ≥0∞, MeasurableSet {x | HasDensity n μ x c}
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the Borel-measurability ingredient of step 8 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 1, 3.2: the upper and lower densities are Borel functions), for an s-finite measure (no local finiteness, so it applies to μ_V, which may give infinite mass to balls meeting ∂U). Notation: ω_n := unitBallVolume n ∈ (0,∞); B̄_ρ(x) := closedBall x ρ; d(x,ρ) := densityRatio n μ x ρ = μ(B̄_ρ(x))/(ω_n·ofReal(ρ)^n); D⁺(x) := limsup_{ρ↓0} d(x,ρ), D⁻(x) := liminf_{ρ↓0} d(x,ρ) (filter 𝓝[>]0 on ℝ).

1. Fixed radius. For ρ ∈ ℝ, x ↦ μ(B̄_ρ(x)) is Borel: the set C_ρ := {(x,y) ∈ ℝ^N × ℝ^N : dist(y,x) ≤ ρ} is closed, hence measurable for the product σ-algebra (which is the Borel σ-algebra, ℝ^N being second countable: Prod.borelSpace), and its section {y : (x,y) ∈ C_ρ} is B̄_ρ(x); for s-finite μ, x ↦ μ({y : (x,y) ∈ C}) is measurable for every measurable C (measurable_measure_prodMk_left). Dividing by the constant ω_n·ofReal(ρ)^n, x ↦ d(x,ρ) is Borel.

2. Rational radii. Fix x and δ > 0; write φ(ρ) := μ(B̄_ρ(x)) (nondecreasing in ρ), ψ(ρ) := ω_n·ofReal(ρ)^n (continuous on (0,∞) with values in (0,∞)), so d(x,ρ) = φ(ρ)/ψ(ρ).
 (a) sup_{ρ∈(0,δ)} d(x,ρ) = sup_{q∈ℚ∩(0,δ)} d(x,q). "≥" is clear. For "≤" let ρ ∈ (0,δ). If φ(ρ) = ∞ then φ(q) = ∞ = d(x,q) for every rational q ∈ (ρ,δ), and such q exist. Otherwise, for rational q ∈ (ρ,δ), d(x,q) = φ(q)/ψ(q) ≥ φ(ρ)/ψ(q), and φ(ρ)/ψ(q) → φ(ρ)/ψ(ρ) = d(x,ρ) as q ↓ ρ through rationals (ψ continuous and positive at ρ, φ(ρ) finite); hence d(x,ρ) ≤ sup_{q∈ℚ∩(0,δ)} d(x,q).
 (b) inf_{ρ∈(0,δ)} d(x,ρ) = inf_{q∈ℚ∩(0,δ)} d(x,q). "≤" is clear. For "≥" let ρ ∈ (0,δ); if φ(ρ) = ∞ then d(x,ρ) = ∞ and there is nothing to prove. Otherwise, for rational q ∈ (0,ρ), d(x,q) = φ(q)/ψ(q) ≤ φ(ρ)/ψ(q) → d(x,ρ) as q ↑ ρ through rationals, so inf_{q∈ℚ∩(0,δ)} d(x,q) ≤ d(x,ρ).

3. Borel densities (first two conjuncts). The intervals (0, 1/(m+1)), m ∈ ℕ, form a basis of 𝓝[>]0, so by Filter.HasBasis.limsup_eq_iInf_iSup / liminf_eq_iSup_iInf and step 2, D⁺(x) = inf_m sup_{q∈ℚ∩(0,1/(m+1))} d(x,q) and D⁻(x) = sup_m inf_{q∈ℚ∩(0,1/(m+1))} d(x,q). These are countable infima/suprema of the Borel functions x ↦ d(x,q) of step 1, hence D⁺ and D⁻ are Borel.

4. Level sets (third conjunct). [0,∞] is a complete linear order with the order topology and 𝓝[>]0 is a nontrivial filter, so d(x,·) → c along 𝓝[>]0 iff D⁻(x) = c and D⁺(x) = c (Filter.Tendsto.liminf_eq, Filter.Tendsto.limsup_eq, tendsto_of_liminf_eq_limsup). Hence {x : HasDensity n μ x c} = D⁺⁻¹({c}) ∩ D⁻⁻¹({c}), the intersection of preimages of the closed (Borel) singleton {c} under Borel maps; it is Borel. ∎
proof_key_steps: x ↦ μ(B̄_ρ(x)) is Borel for s-finite μ (measurable_measure_prodMk_left on the closed set {dist ≤ ρ}).
Monotonicity of ρ ↦ μ(B̄_ρ(x)) and continuity of ω_nρ^n reduce sup/inf over real radii in (0,δ) to rational radii.
limsup and liminf along 𝓝[>]0 are countable inf-sup / sup-inf of Borel functions, hence Borel.
HasDensity n μ x c ⟺ limsup = c ∧ liminf = c, so the level set is Borel.

audit.reason: The type explicitly includes SFinite μ and exactly states all three conclusions. The s-finite product-section theorem proves fixed-radius measurability. The one-sided rational-radius comparisons remain valid with infinite ball masses; countable lattice operations then give measurable upper/lower densities and every density level set, including c = ∞.
